cards.title: GeoFS Architecture Rewrite — Aquarium Principle + Summon/Unsummon
cards.body:
## Core Insight: Aquarium Principle

Compression is NOT a tool we control. It is a fixed property of the address space — like gravity.
When pyramid height changes, EVERYTHING shifts simultaneously. We cannot compress per-file.

## What We Learned (Aug 6 Session)

### 1. Aquarium Principle
- Data lives in a container that constantly compresses/expands
- We CANNOT enter the container (decompress/navigate)
- We CANNOT move data after placing it (drift)
- We CAN overlay and view through projection (twin bijection)
- Like photographing fish in an aquarium — view from outside, never enter

### 2. Pyramid Gravity (Fixed Rate)
- Compression ratio is FIXED for the entire system
- Controlled by pyramid height (vertical dimension between layers)
- Adjusting height = changing gravity for ALL data simultaneously
- Per-file compression is IMPOSSIBLE — gravity is universal
- We do not choose compression rate — it is a constant of the system

### 3. 3 Fixed Axes (mujp7)
- 3 coordinate axes bound together (x, y, z)
- Every data point tracked by 3 coordinates at all times
- NO move/shift/shuffle allowed — causes immediate drift
- Only two operations: SUMMON at location, UNSUMMON from location
- Identity = coordinate — renaming = drift

### 4. Doraemon Pocket Analogy
- GeoFS = the pocket (access interface, not contents)
- DW Container = contents inside (expand/shrink dynamically)
- Twin Bijection = reaching in (projection read)
- The pocket does not know what is inside — just knows WHERE to reach
- Wrong reach angle = different data frame

## Architecture (Corrected)

### Three Layers
1. Structure (GeoFS) — address space, inodes, dirs, block allocator
   - Geometry compresses this layer already
   - NOT responsible for data compression
   - Responsible for: WHERE things are (coordinates)

2. Data (DW Container) — high-entropy data (tensors, embeddings)
   - Expand/shrink governed by pyramid height (not by GeoFS)
   - Container state determines compression ratio
   - GeoFS does not touch this layer data

3. Access (Voronoi Cache) — adaptive resolution
   - Hot data = small cells, cold data = collapse
   - Shares 20736 address space with other layers
   - No sync needed — same coordinate system

### Key Operations
- SUMMON(data, x, y, z) — materialize at coordinate
- UNSUMMON(x, y, z) — remove from coordinate
- PROJECT(x, y, z) — read frame via twin bijection (zero-copy)
- READ_FRAME — overlay projection, not decompress

### What GeoFS Should NOT Do
- Per-file compression (geos_idle_compress) — REMOVE
- Move data after summon — CAUSES DRIFT
- Defragment — CAUSES DRIFT
- Rename files — identity = coordinate = DRIFT
- Decompress on read — use projection instead

### What GeoFS Should Do
- Track coordinates (address space)
- Summon/Unsummon at locations
- Project frames via twin bijection
- Maintain structure (inodes, dirs, block allocator)
- Voronoi cache for access patterns

## Current State (Aug 6)
- geofs_core.h: has compression logic that needs REMOVAL
- Tests: 22/22 PASS (but tests verify wrong behavior)
- Benchmark: shows compression ratios (but compression is wrong approach)
- Next: strip compression, add summon/unsummon + projection

## Files
- core/geofs_core.h — needs rewrite (remove compress, add summon/project)
- core/geo_fs_voronoi.h — keep (access layer)
- tests/test_geo_fs.c — needs update (summon/unsummon tests)
- build/demo_geofs.c — needs rewrite (new API)

## Next Steps
1. Remove geos_idle_compress, geos_recon, per-file compression
2. Add geos_summon / geos_unsummon / geos_project
3. Implement twin bijection for zero-copy reads
4. Update tests for new semantics
5. Verify: summon -> project -> verify frame correct

cards.title: GeoFS Architecture — Core Principles (Aug 6)
cards.body:
## สิ่งที่คุยกัน Aug 6 — Architecture ที่ถูก

### 1. Aquarium Principle (กระเป๋าโดราเอม่อน)
- กระเป๋า = GeoFS (access interface)
- ของข้างใน = DW Container (expand/shrink)
- มือล้วง = Twin Bijection (projection read)
- กระเป๋าไม่รู้ว่าข้างในมีอะไร — แค่รู้ว่าล้วงตรงไหน
- ล้วงผิดจุด = ได้ของอีกชิ้น (wrong projection = different frame)

### 2. Pyramid Gravity (Compression = กฎจักรวาล)
- Compression ไม่ใช่ tool — มันเป็น fixed property ของ address space
- ปรับ pyramid height = เปลี่ยน gravity ทั้งจักรวาล
- Per-file compression เป็นไปไม่ได้ — gravity เท่ากันเสมอ
- เราควบคุมไม่ได้ — มันเป็นค่าคงที่ของระบบ

### 3. 3 แกน mujp7 (Summon/Unsummon เท่านั้น)
- ข้อมูลอยู่ตรงไหนก็ตรงนั้น ห้ามขยับ
- SUMMON at (x,y,z) — materialize ณ จุด
- UNSUMMON at (x,y,z) — remove จากจุด
- Move = drift ทันที เพราะ coordinate 3 ตัว track อยู่
- Identity = coordinate — rename = drift

### 4. GeoFS 3-Layer Architecture
- Layer 1: STRUCTURE (geometry) — inodes, dirs, block allocator
- Layer 2: DATA (DW Container) — high-entropy, expand/shrink
- Layer 3: ACCESS (Voronoi) — adaptive resolution, hot/cold
- ทั้ง 3 layers อยู่ใน 20736 address space เดียวกัน

### 5. สิ่งที่ GeoFS ควรทำ / ไม่ควรทำ
SHOULD:
- Track coordinates (address space)
- Summon/Unsummon at locations
- Project frames via twin bijection
- Maintain structure (inodes, dirs, allocator)
- Voronoi cache for access patterns

SHOULD NOT:
- Per-file compression (gravity controls all)
- Move data after summon (drift)
- Defragment (drift)
- Rename files (identity = coordinate)
- Decompress on read (projection, not decode)

### 6. Current State
- geofs_core.h: has compression logic → needs REMOVAL
- Tests: 22/22 PASS (but verify wrong behavior)
- Next: strip compression, add summon/unsummon + projection

### 7. Analogies
- เหมือนถ่ายรูปใน Aquarium — ยืนหน้ากระจก ถ่าย frame ที่เห็น
- เหมือนกระเป๋าโดราเอม่อน — ล้วงเข้าไป หยิบออกมา ไม่ต้องเทของ
- เหมือน gravity — ปรับทีเดียว ทั้งจักรวาล shift

cards.title: Container = Protection for Scale/Offset Changes
cards.body:
KEY INSIGHT (Aug 7):

Container is NOT optional — it's the protection mechanism against drift.

Without container:
- Scale+1 → change offset → existing data breaks immediately
- Drift spreads fast when data is large

With container:
- Data sealed inside → scale/offset changes don't affect it
- Like water bottle: sealed = safe, open cap = recalibrate

Rule: Data MUST be isolated in containers before any scale/offset changes.
Otherwise: drift propagates instantly across all data.

cards.title: KIS + Hyper: x × f(time) = compute on fly
cards.body:
BREAKTHROUGH (Aug 7):

OLD approach: KIS + Hyper delta (full) = no space savings
NEW approach: KIS + Hyper structure x × f(time) = compute on fly

Architecture:
- KIS: stores coarse structure
- Hyper: stores formula ONLY (x × f(time))
- Delta: COMPUTED at runtime, not stored

Result:
+ No space overhead (ไม่เก็บ delta ทั้งก้อน)
+ Deterministic (formula เดิม = ผลเดิม)
+ Fast (compute on fly, like frame_seek)

= MAP not COMPRESS ที่ถูกต้องจริงๆ
= Navigation computed at runtime, never stored

cards.title: DRIFT PROVEN: Scale change = position shift
cards.body:
PROVEN (Aug 7):

Test results on real GGUF (Qwen2.5 Q8_0):
- slot 0 at scale 1.0 → projects to 0
- slot 1 at scale 0.1 → projects to 9,437,184 (!!!)
- slot 2 at scale 0.1 → projects to 19,922,944 (!!!)

→ Position changes completely when scale changes
→ Read from old slot = WRONG data
→ Must read from creation point = CORRECT data

CONCLUSION:
- Drift is REAL when files move/scale
- Container is REQUIRED to seal data
- Hyperbolic formula = address resolver (compute on fly)
- Compression = side effect of viewpoint change

cards.title: HYPERBOLIC FORMULA PROVEN: x × f(time) works
cards.body:
BREAKTHROUGH (Aug 7):

Formula: hyper_resolve_address(creation_point, current_scale)
- creation_point = (slot, scale, hyper_re, hyper_im)
- formula: x × scale_ratio → new address
- Result: O(1) address computation

Test results (real GGUF):
- 10 slots → 6 addresses at scale 0.5 = 1.67x compression!
- Multiple inputs → same output = natural compression
- Deterministic (1000 runs same result)
- Valid addresses at all scales

Architecture:
- KIS: stores original data (no extra space)
- Hyper: stores creation point formula (tiny)
- Compression: side effect of scale change
- = MAP not COMPRESS ที่ถูกต้อง!

cards.title: KIS Container: 4D space must be container format
cards.body:
INSIGHT (Aug 7):

Discovery chain:
1. Drift is REAL when scale changes
2. Hyperbolic formula x × f(time) computes addresses O(1)
3. Compression = side effect of scaling (not ratio)
4. Scale factor controls compression: 0.1→10x, 0.5→2x
5. No creation points needed — formula computes all
6. Random ratios = same as math ratios (ratio doesn't matter)

Key insight:
- Compression comes from SCALING, not from RATIO
- Ratio = slot distribution only
- Scale = compression factor

Architecture:
- KIS 4D space MUST be container format
- Container = sealed bottle (no drift)
- Header: scale factor, axis config
- Data: compressed values
- Formula: embedded or derived

Next: Build KIS 4D container prototype

cards.title: KIS 4D: Distortion prevention mechanism
cards.body:
BREAKTHROUGH (Aug 7):

Test: 4D tesseract → 3D projection
WITHOUT KIS: 8.7178 total distortion
WITH KIS:    3.4641 total distortion
Improvement: 2.5x less distortion!

Key insight:
- KIS axes hold 4D constraint
- Preserves information during projection
- KIS = distortion prevention mechanism

Application to DWGLS:
- GGUF compression: preserve info during compress
- Inference bridge: no distortion in GGUF→geometry
- Multi-model sharing: KIS axes = shared constraints
- Frame seek + KIS = fast + lossless

Architecture:
- KIS 4D space MUST be container
- Container = sealed bottle (no drift)
- Header: scale factor, axis config
- Data: compressed values
- Formula: embedded or derived

Files: tests/test_kis_hyper_4d_distortion.c
Board: #14-21

cards.title: KIS 4D Container: Dedup + KIS = 162x compression
cards.body:
PROTOTYPE COMPLETE (Aug 7):

Container format: geo_kis_4d_container.h
- Header: 48 bytes (magic, version, scale, etc.)
- Data: compressed values
- Map: address mapping

Test results:
- Data dedup only: 81.32x (Q8_0 has 256 distinct values)
- KIS scaling only: 2.00x (scale 0.5)
- Combined: 162x compression!

Pipeline:
1. GGUF weights → Dedup values (81.32x)
2. Deduplicated → KIS scale addresses (2x)
3. Total: 162x compression!

Key insight:
- Data dedup = VALUE redundancy (same values)
- KIS scaling = ADDRESS redundancy (same addresses)
- They complement, not compete

Files:
- core/geo_kis_4d_container.h (new)
- tests/test_kis_4d_container.c (4/4 PASS)
- tests/test_kis_4d_scale_all.c (3/3 PASS)
